label: Photo stems
summary: Young trees on open ground (rough, semi rough, deep rough, fairway) that the lidar missed, found from their shadows in the summer photo, sized by the lidar stems that cast a shadow there and typed from the leaf-off photo; proposals until accepted in the Vegetation mode (Trees in photo) or with bun run trees:photo, then planted like lidar stems.
steps: Open ground: rough, semi rough, deep rough and fairway minus greens, tees, bunkers, water, creeks, paths, rock slabs, tree areas and the woodland floor, whatever order they were drawn in, with a band kept off them and a wider one off the water (pond-bank stones cast shadows too).
Shadows: on the open ground only, the summer photo's luminance against the open grass round it; a patch darker than shadow-grow with a core darker than shadow-seed is a shadow.

Sun: the shadow direction is the median direction from the lidar stems to the shadows that reach them; the sun factor is a shadow's tip distance per metre of lidar height over the lidar stems whose own shadow ends next to them.
Where: a photo stem stands offset (or offset-per-width x the shadow's width, when more) sun-side of where its shadow ends; never within dedupe-m of a lidar stem or in a lidar tree's own shadow.

Size: height and crown radius as the matched lidar trees have them for that shadow tip distance and width (a least-squares line over them; a thin young crown casts a lighter, shorter-looking shadow); with fewer than min-fit matches the sun factor alone, with fewer than min-matches the defaults.
Kind: in the leaf-off photo a crown dark and green is a conifer, bare branches darker than the ground a broadleaf, nothing to see unknown.
Accepted photo stems are kept in tiles/<site>/tree-stems-photo.json (Regenerate trees leaves them), skipped ones are remembered there too, and gspro.py trees plants the accepted ones with src photo.

rules.text: A shadow in the summer photo has a core darker than this share of the open grass round it ...
... and reaches as far as the photo stays darker than this share.
A shadow ends on the sun side at the first 0.32 m slice across it that is darker than this on the whole (a green crown tuft there is dark too, but less).
Shorter dark patches along the shadow direction are no tree's shadow.
Smaller dark patches are no tree's shadow.
Larger dark patches are a stand or a big tree, which the lidar has.
A shadow's long axis is at least this times its short one ...
... and an elongated one points within this of the shadow direction.
Nothing this close to water (the bank stones cast shadows in the rough).
Nothing this close to a green, tee, bunker, path, rock slab, tree area or the woodland floor.
A photo stem stands this far sun-side of where its shadow ends (a young tree's crown tuft) ...
... or this times the shadow's width when that is more (a wide crown hides the foot of its own shadow).
A smaller dark patch from this far sun-side of a bigger shadow's stem to that shadow's tip is a piece of the same tree (its crown tuft, a broken shadow).
No photo stem within this of a lidar stem.
A lidar stem casts the shadow that starts within this of it (calibration).
With fewer matched lidar stems the photo is sized by the defaults below.
From this many matched lidar stems the photo stems are sized like them (a line from shadow length and width to lidar height and crown radius); fewer, by the sun factor alone.
Shadow direction (compass) when too few lidar stems cast a shadow (Omberg 2025-06-14: 304).
Shadow tip distance per metre of tree height by default (Omberg 2025-06-14: 1.63, a sun about 32° up).
Crown radius per metre of shadow width by default (Omberg 2025-06-14: 0.35).
Lowest photo stem proposed.
Highest photo stem proposed (a longer shadow is a lidar tree's).
Leaf-off photo: a crown darker than this share of the ground round it ...
... covering at least this ...
... and this much greener than the ground, (G - R) / (R + G + B), with a conifer score (greenness-anchors) of conifer-threshold or more, is a conifer (green in April).
Leaf-off photo: else pixels darker than this ...
... over at least this are bare branches, a broadleaf; less, the kind is unknown.
